newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA MUST BEWARE, SAYS WARNE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA MUST BEWARE, SAYS WARNE.

text.p: Shane Warne believes Australia will face a much more resilient England side this summer and insisted on Thursday that Mike Atherton's men should not be underestimated.
Warne took 34 wickets in the last Ashes test series in England in 1993 which Australia won 4-1, but says the touring side will have to work much harder to succeed this time.

"I think a lot of people are writing them off a bit too early. We're not taking them lightly and we're not going to be complacent, that's for sure," said Warne, who sat out the Australians' opening tour fixture against the Duke of Norfolk's XI.
"We're here to try and win every game we play and to really nail the England side, because we think they've got half a chance of beating us."
Some may suspect Warne is simply trying to soften up his intended targets, but the leg-spinner is adamant the series is not a foregone conclusion.

"I've had a lot of success against England, but I think the English players just need to get some team spirit together. They've always had a good side on paper but they haven't been able to do the business on the field."

Warne's varied assortment of deliveries will be closely studied by the English batsmen before the test series starts, but the blond-haired spinner believes staring at videos is not the perfect answer to playing him.
"It can help you get a bit of an idea, but the best thing is to stand behind the net and watch."
Warne, who singled out Jason Gillespie and Matthew Elliott as men the England team should watch out for, realises this summer's test pitches may well suit the seamers more than himself.
For that reason he is reluctant to reveal if he has set himself any personal targets for the series. "If I can take one wicket in each test that changes the game, I'll be happy," he smiled.
